name: Denim boots
description: Mid-calf boots with denim uppers on a rubber sole, a leather band round the top and a zip up the inner side.
notes: A standing pair, 280 mm long and 230 mm tall, toes to +z: denim feet and shafts, a black rubber sole with a short heel, a brown leather top band and a seam band at the ankle; the steel zips face each other on the inner sides. The bounding box of a standing pair takes in the air between and round the boots. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: Faux fur boots
description: Tall soft boots of shaggy synthetic fur on a thick sole, the top turned out in a deep cuff and tied at the ankle with bobbled cords.
notes: A standing pair, 300 mm long and 280 mm tall: khaki cloth feet on a grey sole, grey shaggy shafts with a white fur cuff, khaki cords and bobbles at the ankle front. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The bounding box of a standing pair takes in the air between and round the boots. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: Scrap boots
description: Cloth wrapped round the foot and shin and bound with rag strips, with rusty metal scraps lashed over the toe, the shin and the ankle.
notes: A standing pair, 290 mm long and 200 mm tall: pale rag uppers bound with five darker rag bands, a rusty plate over the toe and another tied over the shin with a bolt, a grey steel patch over each outer ankle, on a black rubber sole. Usage is empty because survivors make them rather than finding them. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The bounding box of a standing pair takes in the air between and round the boots. name: Western boots
description: Tall stiff leather boots with a pointed toe and a stacked heel, the shafts stitched in chevrons. Each shaft has room to hide something small.
notes: A standing pair, 300 mm long and 320 mm tall: narrow pointed brown feet on a walnut-coloured leather sole with a 30 mm heel, black shafts with three cream stitched chevrons down the front, and a brown pull tab either side of the top. The pocket is the space inside one shaft, sized for a small pistol. The bounding box of a standing pair takes in the air between and round the boots. name: Hardened mail chausses
description: Mail booties of hardened steel rings that cover the foot and tie at the top of the leg.
notes: Laid flat as a pair, each a mail leg 120 mm across with its foot turned out to the side, 300 mm from the leather tie to the heel; the hardened steel mail is ridged with rows of rings. Mail slumps flat on the floor rather than standing. The model lays the mail out so it reads as two booties. Usage is empty because they are smithed rather than found. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: Hardened sabaton
description: A shell of jointed hardened steel lames that straps over a shoe to cover the top of one foot.
notes: One sabaton, 280 mm long and 100 mm tall: seven lames alternating hardened and grey steel step down from the ankle to a rounded toe; it is open behind with a dark hollow, held by a leather strap under the arch and a buckled strap round the heel. A sabaton covers one foot, so a player wears two. Slot feet like the other footwear; a sabaton sits on the outer layer over a shoe, which the feet slot cannot yet express. The heel strap loop stands out behind and the box takes in its air. Usage is empty because they are smithed. The xl size shares the model. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: Hardened sheet sabatons
description: A pair of crude foot guards bent from hardened sheet steel and riveted together, strapped over shoes.
notes: A standing pair, 300 mm long and 95 mm tall: three thick plates over the front of each foot, alternating hardened and blackened steel, steel rivets at the sides, open behind, with leather straps under the arch and round the heel. They sit on the outer layer over a shoe, which the feet slot cannot yet express. The heel strap loops stand out behind and the box takes in their air. Usage is empty because they are made rather than found. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.
